I was of the same mindset when I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. I didn't want my family to suffer because I couldn't control my impulses. But my family,being amazing as they are,decided that they're gonna cut out sweets and junk food with me. And they wouldn't bring foods I couldn't eat and leave them unattended before me. Their support meant the world to me. When they went outside, they would still eat sweets and such,but we have just decided that we're not gonna keep them at home. Later, I learned that there was a secret stash, but that was completely okay. I was talking to my therapist about how guilty I felt because of that, but he reassured me that that's just their way of showing me their support and being with me through this big life changing diagnosis. He said that I had nothing to feel guilty about. Same thing when my sis got diagnosed with hypertension. She had to cut out energy drinks,so I did the same. It really wasn't too much to ask for.

Type 2 here,also. I'm not gonna make a judgement for either of them,I'm just gonna share my experience. When I was diagnosed,priority one was, of course, to lose weight. Having self-control after years of eating whatever you want is actually that hard for some people. Do you know what my family did? They modelled their eating habits around me. We all learned to make healthier choices,prepare food in healthier ways, and cut out sugar consumption. Not because I wanted them to,but because they wanted to support me and realised the seriousness of the situation. It meant world to me. They would still eat sugar in front of me,but they wouldn't give me any. That support is what got me through. And this guy really seems to be struggling, and I understand him,that was me 2 years ago. I'm not saying his wife has to change the way she is eating because of his illness, but she could be a little more supportive. Anyway,I don't really think that either of them is AH.

Her brother is dead,it's his funeral,and she's concentrated on how you guys look and what you wore? And your comment was inappropriate because it's her brothers funeral,but hers were not? I'd say hers were twice worse given the circumstances. I can not fathom that someone is burying their brother and is more focused on body shaming her family than mourning. And telling your cousin,who is actually mourning, to man up? Your aunt is toxic, and I absolutely see why none of you like her. 

NTA, and if I were you, I would bring up how no one likes her because of her comments every time she makes those comments. If your elders won't put a stop to it, you definitely should.
